# kitemetric.com - crawler rules.
#
# THE ONE RULE THAT MATTERS: the collateral surfaces must never be indexed by
# any search engine. /biz is the sales card collection and /hr is the HR
# material; both carry an encrypted index, but the CARD IMAGES beside it are
# plain PNG files on a public CDN, and an image cannot carry a <meta> tag. This
# file is what keeps them out of Google Images.
#
# WHY Disallow AND NOT ONLY noindex. For an HTML page you want REMOVED after it
# has been indexed, Disallow is the wrong tool - it stops the crawler fetching
# the page, so the crawler never reads the noindex and the URL can linger. That
# is not this case. Nothing here has ever been indexed, nothing links to it, and
# for IMAGES robots.txt is Google's own documented method of keeping them out of
# image search. So both are used, each where it works:
#
#     the index pages   <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">
#     the card images   this file
#
# DISALLOW IS A PREFIX MATCH. `Disallow: /biz` blocks /biz, /biz/, /biz.html and
# anything else beginning with those characters - including a future /bizdev
# that nobody meant to hide. If you add a public page whose path starts with
# these letters, give it a different name rather than narrowing the rule.
#
# check-noindex.py fails the build if a surface declared private is missing from
# this file, so the two cannot drift apart.

User-agent: *
Disallow: /biz
Disallow: /hr

# THE SITEMAP IS GENERATED, NOT COMMITTED, so do not go looking for
# website/sitemap.xml - there is none. generate-sitemap.py writes it into dist/
# during `make build`, from the pages that are actually in the artifact at that
# point. That ordering is the whole point: the blog is stripped from production
# builds by strip-dev-only.py, and a hand-written sitemap would keep advertising
# it to Google long after the HTML stopped shipping. A generated one cannot,
# because it never sees a page the build did not produce.
#
# Absolute URL because a sitemap directive must be absolute - unlike Disallow,
# it is not resolved against this file's host.
Sitemap: https://kitemetric.com/sitemap.xml
